transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, thank you for seeing me. I'm sorry to take up your time, I know you're probably very busy. 

I guess I'm here because... well, a few people have mentioned that my communication has been a little... confusing lately? I'm an artist, and I write these artist statements and keep notes for clients, and I guess recently when I'm in meetings or writing things down, I've been kind of blending things together. Like, I'll be talking about the texture of a piece, and then suddenly I'm talking about the budget, and then maybe how the colors have these hidden meanings... which makes sense to me, you know? But my clients and colleagues are saying they can't really follow my train of thought. 

It's probably just me being a little too creative or stressed, right? I hope it's not a big deal. Does that make sense?
Over these recent weeks, have you also noticed your mood feeling unusually elevated, euphoric, or irritable, along with having much more energy than usual or needing less sleep than before?

Um... well, I wouldn't say "euphoric," necessarily. That sounds so extreme, right? But I guess... yeah, I've had these stretches where I just feel really, really lit up. Like I have all this energy and every idea I come up with for a project is just brilliant, and I feel almost unstoppable. Which is great for my work, honestly! I get so much done. 

But... well, I suppose I have been a little more on edge, too? Like, if a collaborator makes a tiny comment about a piece, I might... snap a little bit. In a way that's probably bigger than the situation calls for. I don't mean to, I just feel so passionate about the work right now. Is that normal when you're just really focused on a project? I hope I don't sound too difficult to work with.
How long have these periods of feeling 'lit up' with high energy and less need for sleep lasted—days, or at least a full week?

Um... well, it's actually been going on for a little while? I guess... if I really think about it, these stretches where I'm super energized and maybe a bit irritable, running on barely any sleep and juggling way too many projects... they've kind of been a part of my life for about 10 months now? 

I know that sounds like a really long time to be like that, and I hope it doesn't make me sound completely out of control. I've just been so incredibly driven this year. Is it okay to be in that kind of intense creative zone for that long? I always just figured I was having a really productive year.

When you're not in one of these energized, 'lit up' stretches—during times your mood and energy feel more normal—do you still notice your thoughts or speech jumping between unrelated topics, or does that only happen during the high-energy periods?

Um... well, it's a little embarrassing to admit, but... yeah, it still happens even when I'm not feeling super energized. Like, there was this one month, maybe a little while ago, where I was actually sleeping okay? I wasn't feeling that unstoppable rush, and my mood was pretty even, I think. 

But... I guess my thoughts were still a little messy. I didn't want to tell anyone because it sounds so strange, but... even during that quieter month, for a few weeks, I was still... well, I was still hearing these little comments coming from behind the supply shelves in my studio. And I kept seeing these... I don't know, hidden warnings? Like, just in the way the paint tubes were arranged or how the canvas was stretched. It felt so real to me at the time, but I know it sounds a bit odd now. 

I really try to keep it together, though, I promise. I hope that doesn't make me sound too weird? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

During that month when your mood and energy felt normal, how long did the experience of hearing those comments and seeing hidden warnings in your studio last—was it for at least two full weeks in a row?

Um... yeah, it was definitely for at least two weeks. Maybe even three? It was during that whole quiet month I mentioned, where I was sleeping okay and not feeling that huge rush of energy. 

I really hope I don't sound completely crazy saying this, but... yeah, for several weeks straight, I just kept hearing those little voices or comments coming from behind the shelves. And I couldn't stop seeing those... those hidden warnings in the studio materials, like the paint tubes and stuff. I tried so hard to ignore it and just focus on my work, because I know how it sounds. It's not like I wanted to be distracted by it. Is it okay that I'm telling you this? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a distinct manic episode (elevated/expansive energy, decreased need for sleep, irritability, grandiosity about creative abilities) lasting approximately 10 months, meeting duration criteria for mania. Concurrently, she describes disorganized speech/thought (tangential, loosely associated topics) and psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations of voices behind shelves, delusional perception of 'hidden warnings' in objects). Critically, these psychotic symptoms persisted for at least 2-3 weeks during a period when mood and energy were euthymic/normal, establishing that psychotic symptoms occur independently of the mood episode—a core diagnostic requirement for schizoaffective disorder distinguishing it from a mood disorder with psychotic features (e.g., bipolar disorder with psychotic features, F31.2) where psychosis is confined to mood episodes. The combination of a full manic episode plus psychotic symptoms present without mood symptoms for a substantial period supports schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type (F25.0), coded here as F25.
